# Draft:Uyghur woman's chay culture

}}
In Uyghur culture, the chay party is a part of women's daily social activities and functions in tandem with cultural inheritance, moral education and economic exchanges.
Uyghur women's chay gatherings are usually organized by family members, friends, or community members to share tea, food, and various forms of entertainment.
Description and function
The chay party is one of the important occasions for Uyghur women to socialize. Participants usually sit together and talk about daily life, family affairs and social developments. Such gatherings not only enhance community cohesion, but also provide a platform for women to support each other.
The chay party is also an important place for oral culture and moral education. Older women often teach the younger generation traditional knowledge of household management, etiquette, and crafts, and discuss social norms and values at chay parties.
At the Uyghur women's chay party, music, dance, story telling (Dastan) and poetry recitation are among the core elements.
Types
Uyghur women's chay parties can be divided into different types, mainly including family chay parties, social chay parties and traditional chay parties (Meshrep).
Family
Family members and relatives gather together to exchange daily affairs over chay. This form of chay party is usually more casual and is an important part of Uyghur family life.
Social
Social chay parties are organized by communities or groups of friends and are usually held on specific occasions such as festivals, wedding eve or celebrations. Such chay parties not only promote social interaction, but may also involve discussions about marriage, parenting and health.
Traditional (Meshrep)
Meshrep is a more formal form of chay party that has a strong cultural and moral educational function. Traditionally, the host (Yigit Bashi) is responsible for organizing the event and ensuring that established rules of etiquette are followed. In Meshrep, participants may discuss social issues, resolve conflicts within the community, and engage in cultural activities such as singing, dancing, and storytelling.
Meslehet Chay
Before the wedding, the Uyghur community would hold a "Meslehet Chay" (consultation chay party). The couple and their relatives and friends discuss the wedding ceremony and related arrangements at the chay party, and accept the blessings of relatives and friends. This chay party is both a planning meeting for family affairs and an important social event to strengthen kinship.
Chay Puli
A form of economic exchange called "Chay Puli" (chay party money) has emerged in modern Uyghur family chay parties. In a fixed circle of friends and family, one member of each chay party is the "Chay Bashi" (chay party organizer), and the other members give Chay Puli in different amounts according to their own financial circumstances and wishes. For example, four people A, B, C and D regularly participate in the chay party, and this time Chay Bashi is D. A may give 100 yuan, B may give 200 yuan, and C may give 300 yuan, adding up to a total sum of 600 yuan. D will record the amount given by each person. In the next chay party, if A becomes Chay Bashi, D only has to give 100 yuan back to A, and if B becomes chay bashi, D will give 200 yuan back to B. This model ensures that each participant ends up paying the same amount as he or she receives, while at the same time ensuring that each member receives a larger sum of money in a given month for investment or large spending, thus acting as a mutual financial aid.
